## Summary

We will construct the design stage model using aggregate-level data to predict attrition rates based on trial design features while accounting for differences in trial duration. The model will be similar to that described in NICE Technical Support Document 3 (3.2. Rate data: Binomial likelihood and cloglog link) for modelling rates where event times are not available.

## Data

```{r makedata}
library(tidyverse)
mydf <- tibble(trial_id = paste0("NCT", sample(1000000:9999999, 4)),
               r = c(25, 10, 73, 91),
               N = c(1000, 500, 2000, 700),
               t = c(26, 52, 36, 12),
               arm_type = c("Placebo", "Active", "Active", "Placebo"),
               blinding = c("Single", "Double", "Triple", "Double"),
               phase = c(3L, 4L, 3L, 3L),
               other_covariates = c("...", "...", "...", "..."))

mydf %>% knitr::kable()

```

## Model description

For each trial $i$, we will specify the model likelihood using the binomial distribution:

\begin{aligned}
r_i \sim binom(\theta_i, N_i) \\
\end{aligned}

Where $i$ indicates a trial, $r$ represents the observed number of attrition events, $\theta$ represents the probability of attrition at time $t$ and $N$ represents the number of participants in trial $i$. 

Informed by findings from our previous IPD analysis of attrition rates (i.e. rates described well by Gompertz time-to-event models), we will use the Gompertz cumulative distribution function as a link function for $\theta_i$:

\begin{aligned}
F(t_i) &= 1 - \exp \left(-\frac{a_i}{b_i} \exp(b_i t_i) \right),
\end{aligned}

where $a \geq 0$ is the shape parameter and $b \geq 0$ is the rate parameter for trial $i$ at time $t$.

We will treat covariates as fixed effects over all trials and place covariates on $a$:

\begin{aligned}
\log(a_i) = \beta_{0i} + \beta_{1i}X_{1i} + \dots + \beta_{ki}X_{ki},
\end{aligned}

where $\beta_{0i}$ is a fixed intercept, $\beta_{1i} \dots \beta_{ki}$ are coefficients estimated for covariates and $X_{1i} \dots X_{ki}$ are the covariates.

We will specify random intercepts (i.e. across trials) for $b$:

\begin{aligned}
b_i = \exp(\beta_{0i} + u_i),
\end{aligned}

where $\beta_{0i}$ is the baseline hazard for trial $i$ and $u_i$ is a random intercept.

## Model code (without coefficient shrinkage)

``` stan
data {
  int<lower=0> N; // number of participants
  int<lower=0> r[N]; // observed attrition events
  int<lower=0> n[N]; // number of trials
  vector[N] dt; // time in weeks
  vector[N] var1; // example var
}

parameters {
  real mu1; // intercept
  real beta; // coefficient
  real a_raw; // raw shape parameter
}

transformed parameters {
  real a; // shape
  vector[N] b; // rate
  vector[N] p; // attrition probability
  
  a = a_raw == 0 ? 0.0001 : a_raw; // ensure shape is not exactly zero
  for (i in 1:N) {
    b[i] = exp(mu1 + var1[i] * beta);
    p[i] = 1 - exp(-b[i] / a * (exp(a * dt[i]) - 1));
  }
}

model {
  mu1 ~ normal(0, 1); // Intercept prior
  beta ~ normal(0, 1); // Normal prior for coefficient
  a_raw ~ normal(0, 1); // Normal prior for shape
  
  // likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
    r[i] ~ binomial(n[i], p[i]);
  }
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N] r_new; // predicted count
  vector[N] p_new; // predicted probability of attrition
  
  for (i in 1:N) {
    p_new[i] = 1 - exp(-b[i] / a * (exp(a * dt[i]) - 1));
    r_new[i] = binomial_rng(n[i], p_new[i]);
  }
  real rate = exp(mu1); // transformed rate
}
```

## Model code (with coefficient shrinkage)

A common laplace prior will be placed on coefficients to allow for shrinkage towards zero.

``` stan
data {
  int<lower=0> N; // number of participants
  int<lower=0> r[N]; // observed attrition events
  int<lower=0> n[N]; // number of trials
  vector[N] dt; // time in weeks
  vector[N] var1; // example var
}

parameters {
  real mu1; // intercept
  real beta_raw; // raw coefficient
  real<lower=0> tau_beta; // scale parameter for coefficient shrinkage
  real a_raw; // raw shape parameter
}

transformed parameters {
  real a; // shape
  vector[N] b; // rate
  vector[N] p; // attrition probability
  real beta = beta_raw * tau_beta; // coefficient with shrinkage
  
  a = a_raw == 0 ? 0.0001 : a_raw; // ensure shape is not exactly zero
  for (i in 1:N) {
    b[i] = exp(mu1 + var1[i] * beta);
    p[i] = 1 - exp(-b[i] / a * (exp(a * dt[i]) - 1));
  }
}

model {
  mu1 ~ normal(0, 1); // Intercept prior
  tau_beta ~ exponential(1); // Shrinkage prior
  beta_raw ~ normal(0, 1); // Normal prior for coefficient
  a_raw ~ lognormal(0, 1); // Lognormal prior for shape
  
  // likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
    r[i] ~ binomial(n[i], p[i]);
  }
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N] r_new; // predicted count
  vector[N] p_new; // predicted probability of attrition
  
  for (i in 1:N) {
    p_new[i] = 1 - exp(-b[i] / a * (exp(a * dt[i]) - 1));
    r_new[i] = binomial_rng(n[i], p_new[i]);
  }
  real rate = exp(mu1); // transformed rate
}
```
